memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Set apart for the Lord your God every firstborn male of your herds and flocks. Do not put the firstborn of your cows to work, and do not shear the firstborn of your sheep. Each year you and your family are to eat them in the presence of the Lord your God at the place he will choose. - Deut 15:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God claims the firstborn of the herds and flocks as His own — set apart to Him, not put to work for personal profit. The firstborn represented the first and often the best of the animals, and God asked that this be dedicated to Him. This was a way of acknowledging that everything belonged to God and that He deserved the first and finest, not the leftovers. Giving God the firstborn was an act of worship, declaring, "You come first."

There is a heart principle here that reaches across the ages. What we give God first reveals what we truly treasure. When we offer Him our best — our first and finest time, energy, and resources — we declare that He holds first place in our lives. When we give Him only leftovers, we reveal that other things have taken priority. God is worthy of our first and best, because He is first in worth.

The firstborn theme runs through Scripture and finds its climax in Christ, who is called "the firstborn over all creation" and "the firstborn from among the dead" (Col 1:15, 18). God gave His own firstborn Son as the ultimate offering, holding nothing back. In response, we give Him our best, not to earn His favor but as grateful worship. This is not about a rigid ritual but about the posture of a heart that puts God first. What does it look like for you to give God your "firstborn" — the first and best of what you have? Offer Him your best today, as an act of worship to the One who gave His best for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What do I give God first — my best, or my leftovers?
- What does my giving reveal about what I truly treasure?
- How does God giving His firstborn Son shape the way I offer Him my best?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are worthy of my first and best, for You gave Your own firstborn Son, holding nothing back. Help me put You first in my time, energy, and resources — not offering leftovers, but my finest, as an act of grateful worship to You. Amen.
